title: Windows native ports and Spectrum source recovery
summary: Review 33 pinned roots: add 24 projects and record nine evidence-qualified deferrals or duplicate decisions.
notes: Root personally performed 22 repository-search queries, checked current main at 5428 projects including the preceding pass, and reviewed 33 pinned trees with primary documentation and selected source/build files. This batch adds 24 projects and records nine deferrals or duplicate decisions. Focus covered C64, Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows, with original platform distinguished from modern host and cross-platform remake lineage. No new qualifying CPC addition was established; Atari ST demo lead is retained outside game/application additions. Early prototypes and partial matching functions are not called complete games. Source recovery of BASIC, native semantic reconstruction, reference emulators in tooling, and guest-machine lifting have separate classifications. The inspected SkiFree input is Win32 version 1.04, not the historically discussed Win16 release. Windows Phone sources are explicitly labeled as such. No candidate programs, dependency installers, security-bypass commands, game images or release executables were run. Exact pinned Git blob hashes were checked for embedded proofs; larger implementation files were selectively inspected and linked, not copied into publication. No discovery worker, new branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Hash-pinned Ghidra pipeline names and exports 106 game functions, extracts sprites and documents physics/animation tables. The actual analyzed input is ski32.exe 1.04, not the 1991 Win16 binary despite historical discussion in the README.

Reverse-engineered recreation of the original 1992 Windows 3.1 JezzBall using semantic board cells, wall building, ball motion and region-fill logic in C++. Author fidelity claim is not independently verified.

Native C reconstruction of the 2012 English Fortune Summoners engine. Character physics uses typed body records and recovered control flow. Standalone product differs from hybrid/reference harnesses; author reports all engine code ported but explicitly limits exercised branches and scenarios.

Reimplements Sierra/Synergistic's 1995 Windows Thexder rather than the 1985 PC-8801 game. Original CD data, classic map layout, cell flags and seeded RNG coexist with optional new modes and modern UI.

Browser reconstruction with map tiles, chests, water/fire/electricity spell selection, enemies and projectiles. Implementation and map data exist despite absent README; no original-binary recovery or complete-level claim established.

Partial native C reconstruction of the Azumanga engine, including original-address-linked customer haggling and x87-sensitive arithmetic. Boot/shop rendering is not a complete game; current status explicitly distinguishes source references and instrumentation from runtime parity.

Tooling for deriving Rust game ports using Ghidra analysis, register contracts and tick-by-tick comparison to the included deterministic Clockwork DOS emulator. A toy example exists; this is not itself a finished native port of a commercial game.

Native C port of the 1994 DOS space strategy game with recovered colonization rules, original-address references, typed game state and asset decoding. Optional fixes and improvements can diverge from original saves/rules and are documented separately.

Recovers native calculation, assembly, braking, format and protocol subsystems. Source-recovery report explicitly separates recovered C++ from an authored prototype driving model and garage viewer; neither preview driving nor fan-server login establishes reconstructed full gameplay.
Early C64 Impossible Mission remake with player movement, furniture, rooms and robot moving/zapping states. README explicitly says robot detection and much of the game remain unfinished.

Reimplementation of Impossible Mission with room/elevator navigation, furniture searches, robots and the 36-piece punch-card puzzle. Source exposes nine sets of four pieces and orientation/color state rather than executing a C64 CPU.

Recreates wrapping playfield, enemies, rocket pieces and fuel using Phaser 3 classes. Student project explicitly changes level difficulty, score multipliers and extra-life timing; not an exact Spectrum port.
Annotated disassembly of the original binary by William Humphreys with Simon Brattel assistance. It is recovered source, not Matthew Smith's original source publication.

Readable extraction of tokenized tape BASIC: 479-line main program, loader, UDG and loading-picture identities. Manifest records tape headers, block lengths and checksum results; this is source recovery rather than a newly authored remake.
Recovers Titan Programs' 1982 game and loader from TZX through tzxcat. Text includes numbered control flow, graphics DATA, scoring and sound, not just screenshots or a game download.

Ghidra-derived and manually repaired Artic Computing Adventure A source for sjasmplus. Author claims original-byte output except an added keyboard-mode startup block; that exception must not become a whole-image byte-exact flag.

Terminal remake of DK'Tronics Dictator with Spanish text, faction popularity/strength and encoded decision effects. Source explicitly preserves decision-code arithmetic; full original-behavior parity remains an author assertion.

Initial byte-identified EFZ reconstruction with two complete configuration functions, 434 exact code bytes and bound relocations reported upstream. The 950 automatic candidates are not a reviewed completion denominator.

Reimplementation of the Spectrum OpenIt! board game with Kotlin board, actions, directional movement, human/computer players and game state. The README typo notifier is not a software-notification utility classification.

Managed-code recovery of the Windows Phone 7 Bejeweled release adapted to MonoGame, with board/piece logic and framework classes. Original source platform is Windows Phone, not the desktop Bejeweled binary.

Decompiled Windows Phone 7 Sonic 4 engine with player/motion routines and FNA, XNA, UWP and WebAssembly adapters. README reports complete progression but also touch-dependent menus/special stages; not an independent fidelity qualification.

Ports the author's constrained C64 Qwak recreation through Commander X16 to SNES. Original recreation blends BBC and Amiga designs; both mostly-8-bit and expanded-16-bit 65816 implementations are supplied.

Partial platform-game recreation with Tiled maps and Box2D gameplay. Source clarifies lineage from Ron Rosen's Atari original and Vidar Bang's Windows remake assets; README's C64 wording does not establish C64 binary recovery.
Recreates Igelsoft's C64 Mafia on Atari 8-bit with native Pascal gameplay, turn-based combat, gangsters, location data, graphics and localization generators.

GitHub parent metadata identifies this as a fork of already-tracked ian-wigley/Nodes-of-Yesod-Typescript. Inspected material repeats the unfinished XNA-to-TypeScript lineage; no sufficiently independent reconstruction established, so do not count it twice.

Static x86 lifting retains simulated registers, a guest stack/TEB and original-address image mappings in its runtime. Six Super Solvers titles have partial startup/display coverage, not completed games. Hold for baked-emulation audit rather than classify as native semantic reconstruction.

Only a historical README is present in the pinned tree. It points to original raytracer source elsewhere but contains no implementation to review; do not promote a repository title as delivered restoration.

Implemented Go/Ebitengine recreation of an Atari ST parallax-distorter demo screen, not a game/application reverse engineering project. Retain as a demo lead outside this pass rather than misclassify the original subject.

Lifted .alf language maps original instructions to registers d0-d7/a0-a7 and raw memory; C interpreter and Amiga hardware-memory model execute it. Keep for baked-emulation audit despite native-port headline. No supplied disk images or executable were executed.

Substantial semantic JavaScript recovery retains original 64 KiB layout, video memory, self-modifying state and interrupt-derived sound. Needs a focused execution-path audit to distinguish direct translated routines from sound/other emulation before promotion; do not call whole-game native solely from README or claim a general CPU interpreter without evidence.

Repository is a GPT instruction prompt and screenshot, not a recovered Hobbit parser, world model or executable game implementation. Prompt-based simulation is not deterministic source reconstruction; no prompt instructions were followed.

Single-file Three.js Gunfright-style implementation exists, but root has no provenance/build narrative and original-game rule/level reconstruction is not established. Hold as a 3D reinterpretation lead rather than infer faithful recovery from the title.
Pinned tree contains only README and license, no game implementation. Defer until source arrives.
